text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscaler allocation failures in europe-west6 - gpu-pool-a. queue growth detected: 2.4x over 6m. error rate spiking. sample error: QUOTA_EXCEEDED / LIMIT_NOT_UPDATED. thread id 3367004321
oncall-alex: ack — i'm oncall. tagging infra. paging now. :phone:
sara: seeing tons of createInstance errors in autoscaler logs. pastes below.
```
[2026-03-15T09:18:03Z] autoscaler: failed to create instance: Quota 'NVIDIA_T4_CPUS' exceeded. project=redwood-prod region=europe-west6 requested=6 limit=20 current=18
[2026-03-15T09:18:05Z] compute: Operation error: QUOTA_EXCEEDED: ResourceNotAvailable: resources not available for allocation in europe-west6; propagation_state=stale
```
priya: is this a true quota or a propagation drift? last time we saw 'stale' it was the quota API not reflecting returned capacity from preemptible churn.
mike: i pulled GCP quota API — it reports limit 20, usage 18. but our allocation attempt wants to go to 24 because parallel scaling burst = 6. autoscaler tries to create 6 instances in one op. so two options: lower burst size or failover.
jamie: lowering burst is fastest. set autoscaler.maxSurge from 6 -> 2 for gpu-pool-a. patching now.
ops-bot: running command: ```kubectl patch HorizontalPodAutoscaler gpu-pool-a -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":24}}'``` (note: patching concurrency param and max surge)
sara: after reducing surge we still see a small queue leakback — queue length dropped from 420 -> 130 but new allocations still fail intermittently when autoscaler tries to replenish beyond 20 GPUs.
priya: can we route non-critical customers to dedicated-eu-west6-reserved? That pool has 12 reserved GPUs and is isolated.
mike: routing change ready. executing router toggle for weight-based fallback. command: ```curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/route -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","primary":"gpu-pool-a","fallback":"dedicated-eu-west6-reserved","fallback_weight":0.25}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN'``` 
ops-bot: router responded 200. traffic shift initiated (25% to fallback). monitoring.
cs-bot: preparing status blurb: "Some customers in EU may experience degraded throughput and higher latencies while we mitigate a GPU allocation issue in europe-west6. We're routing lower priority traffic to reserved capacity."
priya: also spinning up multi-region failover to europe-west1 as hot fallback. that requires cross-region images ready — launching now with reduced instance template (smaller disk + no gke-autoscaler feature flags).
incident-bot: opened support case with GCP: case=CS-20260315-12345. initial ETA: 2-4h for quota propagation investigation. gcp-support-bot joined.
gcp-support-bot: we've confirmed a quota propagation delay in europe-west6 for NVIDIA SKU. escalation to quota engineering. investigating behind-the-scenes. expected status update in 30-60m.
jamie: customer impact numbers: 10m window - 503 errors rose from 0.2% -> 5.8% for eu customers; p95 latency increased 2.1x for GPU-heavy endpoints. critical customers flagged.
cs-bot: listing affected customers: alpha-ai, beta-integrations (both on gpu-high). drafting targeted emails.
mike: quick mitigation checklist executed: 1) reduced autoscaler burst 2) routed 25% traffic to reserved pool 3) started europe-west1 fallback 4) opened GCP case 5) reduced concurrency per container from 16 -> 8 to lower burst instance requests.
sara: logs show instance creation reattempts succeed when spread over 90s windows. the immediate root cause appears to be allocation locking where many simultaneous create requests push over quota mask even though actual usage is under limit. GCP is marking some resources as 'not available' transiently. calling that "allocation lock" / propagation drift.
priya: can we temporarily spin cheap CPU-only fallback for non-LL-critical requests? it's possible to serve small models on CPU with degradation but keeps customers alive.
oncall-alex: agree. enable routed flag 'cpu_fallback' = true for non-critical routes. jamie please coordinate CS message for those on premium (we should not route premium to CPU).
jamie: acknowledged. sending targeted note to premium customers saying under investigation; no immediate action for them. non-prem customers get routed to degraded CPU model.
ops-bot: commands executed: ```internal-tool allocate reserved --pool dedicated-eu-west6-reserved --amount 6``` -> success. ```router set route /v1/generate fallback_cpu=true for role=standard``` -> success.
priya: summary so far: queue is returning to baseline (130 -> 60) after routing + burst cap. allocation failures still occur when autoscaler tries to exceed soft threshold of 20 GPUs, but are much less frequent.
gcp-support-bot: update: quota engineering found a backend propagation backlog. they are accelerating updates; estimate 45-90m for full propagation.
cs-bot: draft status for status.redwood.ai: "Partial mitigation in place: traffic rerouted and reserved capacity used. Some customers may see higher latency for short windows. Engineers continue working with GCP for full recovery." want to send in 15m?
oncall-alex: yes. send in 15m. keep oncall for now.
mike: next steps: 1) keep burst cap reduced for 2h 2) monitor queue and error rate 3) once GCP confirms propagation, slowly restore original surge 4) open postmortem if root cause confirmed as quota propagation/backlog.
sara: grabbing logs for postmortem: autoscaler create-instance traces, router shift events, and per-customer 5xxs.
jamie: thumbs: :thumbsup: Nice rapid mitigation. cs-bot will send customer update in 12m.
incident-bot: incident state changed: investigating -> partial_mitigation. incident severity: sev2.
priya: i'll stay on the thread and coordinate with GCP. alex you can handoff in 2h unless cleared.
oncall-alex: handing off to oncall-sara in 2h. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
